content.text: The text reviews intestinal obstruction, including intussusception, fecal impaction, strictures, adhesions, tumors, volvulus, hernias, and functional paralysis. Acute obstruction causes severe colicky pain, vomiting, distension, constipation, collapse, peritonitis, and possible gangrene; chronic disease produces progressive constipation, alternating diarrhea, wasting, and eventual occlusion. Diagnosis relies on history, palpation, rectal examination, and assessing tumors or fecal masses. Historical treatment emphasizes opium, enemas, cautious supportive care, and early laparotomy when mechanical obstruction persists, with enterotomy or colotomy for selected chronic cases. The text then covers intestinal cancer, lardaceous degeneration, rectal and anal diseases, fissures, ulcers, abscesses, fistulas, hemorrhoids, prolapse, strictures, parasites, and their historical treatments. Sandra travelled to the garden. John travelled to the bedroom.
